subject: Plotting RRPP output for analysis of chemical data

messages.author: 976bc48bd89fe0f0
messages.subject: Plotting RRPP output for analysis of chemical data
parts:
Hi all,

I have a few questions about plotting the output of an RRPP analysis. I’m very new to multivariate phylo comparative methods and a lot of this is going way over my head.

I’m assessing the influence of aridity (continuous variable) and habitat use (saxicoline vs. terrestrial) on pheromone blends. The pheromone data consists of 34 logit transformed chemical proportions. My model is:

lm.rrpp( pheromones ~ aridity * habitat, Cov=vcv.phy )

The analysis shows a significant influence of both aridity and habitat, but no significant interaction of the two. I’d like to plot these results but am unsure how best to go about this using the RRPP output.

I tried something along the lines of the multivariate Plethodon shape~size example on the lm.rrpp help page and in Appendix 2 of the methods paper. But I noticed that using the code from this example creates a plot that shows a relationship between PC1 and the alphabetical order of the row names of the predictor. This happens both in the plethodon example and in my own data (when aridity is the predictor; habitat use is ok). I assume the names have been mismatched with the predictor values on the plot somehow? 

Also, in the case of this plot, do the loadings for PC1 correspond to the coefficients for the respective predictor (e.g., aridity) in the model?


Cheers,
Stephen

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Plotting RRPP output for analysis of chemical data
parts:
Stephen,

Could you provide a little more information?  What exactly are you trying to plot?  The model fit?  Maybe provide a little code for your plot attempt so we can know what you have attempted.  It sounds like maybe you are making diagnostic (residual) plots or plots of predicted values, but I can’t be sure without more description.

Thanks!
Mike
